passage: My study group keeps pushing that timer method: 25 minutes of work, a 5-minute break, repeat. I looked it up, and it started with one university student and a tomato-shaped kitchen timer. That's a dorm-room hack, not a real study method, so I'm not reorganizing finals week around it. Back to the library.
cue: That's a dorm-room hack, not a real study method
explanation: Maddie dismisses the timer method because it began as one student's kitchen-timer trick. Humble beginnings don't tell us whether timed work blocks help people focus; only how well it works can.

whyNot.fal_ad_hominem: Maddie isn't attacking the student who invented it or her study group; she judges the method purely by how it started.

passage:
Sofia: Feeling rough. Making Grandma's ginger-lemon tea and staying in tonight.
Leo: That tea thing is just village folklore from before anyone knew what germs were. Hard to take seriously.
Sofia: The warm drink is soothing my throat right now, Leo.
Leo: Folklore is folklore.
cue: just village folklore from before anyone knew what germs were
explanation: Leo dismisses the tea because the remedy began as old folk practice. Where a remedy started doesn't settle whether a warm drink soothes a sore throat; that's a question about its effects.

whyNot.fal_ad_hominem: Leo isn't attacking Sofia or Grandma personally; he rejects the remedy because of where it came from.

title: Re: No-meeting Wednesdays
passage: Hi all, I'm open to fewer meetings, and Felipe's survey (68% of us say meetings break up deep work) deserves a real look. But I should mention that this whole idea started as a joke slide at last year's offsite. I'm wary of reorganizing our week around something that began as a punchline. Maybe we revisit next quarter? Hana
cue: I'm wary of reorganizing our week around something that began as a punchline
explanation: Hana acknowledges the survey, then sets the proposal aside because it first appeared as a joke. How an idea started doesn't tell us whether it would help the team now.

whyNot.fal_ad_hominem: Hana isn't attacking Felipe or whoever made the slide; she judges the idea by its joking origin.

title: Comfy ring, silly score
passage: The Orbet ring is comfortable enough to sleep in and the battery really does last a week. The app's 'readiness score' is mostly built on heart rate variability, though, and HRV was first used to monitor babies during labor. I'm a 42-year-old adult, not a fetus. Not letting that number tell me whether to run. Three stars.
cue: HRV was first used to monitor babies during labor
explanation: Andre likes the hardware but rejects the score because heart rate variability was first used in monitoring births. A measure's first use doesn't decide whether it's useful for adults today.

whyNot.fal_guilt_by_association: Andre isn't objecting to who uses or promotes HRV now; he dismisses it because of where it was first applied.

source: Resident Clara Osei · Larkmoor planning meeting
passage: I've looked at the county's crash data for Mill Road, and I agree that intersection is a problem. But remember how this roundabout plan began: Vellacott Homes drew it up in 2019 to speed traffic into their new subdivision. A plan born to sell houses isn't a plan for this neighborhood, however the county's engineers have dressed it up since.
cue: A plan born to sell houses isn't a plan for this neighborhood
explanation: Clara rejects the roundabout because a developer first drew it up for its own reasons. The county's engineers have since reworked it, so its origin doesn't show whether it would fix the crash problem.

whyNot.fal_guilt_by_association: Vellacott isn't a current backer tainting the plan; Clara rejects it because of how it originated in 2019.

title: Second trial backs afternoon naps for memory in older adults
passage: An independently funded trial at Marrowfield University has confirmed earlier findings that a 20-minute afternoon nap improved recall in adults over 60. Sleep coach Martin Feld isn't persuaded: 'This whole line of research was started by a mattress company looking for a marketing hook. I don't care how many times they rerun it.'
cue: This whole line of research was started by a mattress company looking for a marketing hook
explanation: Martin waves off an independent replication because the research line began with a mattress maker. Funding worries are fair for a single sponsored study, but this new trial had no such ties.

whyNot.fal_ad_hominem: Martin doesn't attack the Marrowfield researchers; he rejects their result because of how the research area began.

passage:
Gabe: Is school really closing at noon Friday? My sister-in-law forwarded a screenshot.
Priti: That screenshot is from an account nobody can identify, and the district website and Ms. Tran's newsletter both list normal hours. So a normal day is far more likely.
Gabe: Fair enough, I'll plan for regular pickup.
cue: the district website and Ms. Tran's newsletter both list normal hours
explanation: Priti discounts the screenshot because its source can't be identified, then checks two official sources that contradict it. Her conclusion rests on that evidence, not on origin alone.

whyNot.fal_genetic_fallacy: For an unverified rumor the source is the evidence, and Priti backs her doubt with official sources instead of dismissing it by origin alone.

title: Phone ban in Lab 2: time to retire it?
passage: Our no-phones rule in Lab 2 dates to 1998, when the old spectrometers were sensitive to radio interference. Those units were replaced in 2021, and the new manufacturer's spec sheet says phones at normal distance have no measurable effect. I asked around and no one knows of any other reason for the rule, so it no longer serves its purpose.
cue: the new manufacturer's spec sheet says phones at normal distance have no measurable effect
explanation: Ngozi traces the rule's origin, then checks whether that reason still applies and looks for other reasons. The rule falls because current evidence removes its only justification.

whyNot.fal_genetic_fallacy: Ngozi doesn't reject the rule for its origin; she tests the original reason against current evidence and finds nothing else supporting it.
